name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: This requires an Emirati citizen father — citizenship is attributed automatically at birth regardless of birthplace.

requirement_groups.name: Child of an Emirati mother (since October 2017)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires an Emirati citizen mother and a foreign father — not automatic; historically required an application once the child reached age 6, subject to specific conditions.
requirements.fix_path: Submit the application once eligibility conditions are met.

requirement_groups.name: Foreign wife of an Emirati man

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 7 years of marriage to an Emirati man if there is a child of the marriage, or 10 years without a child — subject to renouncing prior nationality.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate and evidence of the qualifying parent's Emirati nationality

sources.title: Emirati nationality - The Official Platform of the UAE Government (Federal Law No. 17 of 1972)

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL CONTRAST with ae_citizenship_naturalisation: dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE here (the general rule) — only the narrow exceptional-merit nomination route permits dual citizenship, making the UAE's two citizenship pathways operate under genuinely DIFFERENT nationality-retention rules, a real internal inconsistency worth flagging prominently in any comparison view. Mother-line transmission is confirmed but NOT automatic the way father-line transmission is — a genuine gender asymmetry still present in current law despite the October 2017 reform that first introduced the mother-line pathway at all; historically required an application once the child reached age 6, subject to specific conditions not fully itemized at tier-1 precision during this research pass. Foreign-wife naturalization (7 or 10 years depending on whether there's a child) requires renouncing prior nationality — falling under the standard, more restrictive dual-citizenship rule, not the exceptional-merit route's more permissive one.
